Priya: hey team :wave: trying to run a local streaming demo with a hosted key and it keeps dropping with 429s (rate_limit_exceeded). Is that expected for dev machines?
Sam (DevEx): welcome Priya! short answer: yes, hosted keys are in tighter rate buckets and may be subject to org IP rules. For iterative local dev use the sandbox key or a CI token.
Priya: ok good to know. sandbox supports streaming?
Sam (DevEx): yep, sandbox supports streaming but with lower quota and smaller bursts. Its intended for interactive dev/tests.
Riley: another gotcha: SDKs auto-batch/retry differently than raw REST, which can change observed 429 behavior. If youre hitting 429s with streaming try SDK debug mode + smaller batch settings.
Priya: how do I swap keys for my script? my app reads REDWOOD_API_KEY from env.
Sam (DevEx): simplest: export REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk-sandbox-xxxxx" locally. Example curl (streaming):
```bash
export REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk-sandbox-xxxxx"
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-lite-1","input":"test"}'
```
Priya: is it safe to keep the sandbox token in a .env file on my laptop?
Sam (DevEx): sensible for local dev but never commit it. Add .env to .gitignore and prefer OS keyring or local secrets manager if available. For CI use ephemeral CI tokens from the Console (Service tokens -> CI token) so you don't store long-lived hosted keys in CI.
Priya: my local tests still hit a burst limit. how do I request more sandbox quota for a demo?
Sam (DevEx): file a request at https://redwood.internal/devex/keys-requests or email devex@redwood.ai with: team, repo, expected qps, start/end times. We can grant temporary bursts for scheduled demos.
Luis (IT-Sec): FYI if your org has IP whitelisting enabled, hosted keys from dynamic dev IPs or VPN egress might be blocked causing 429s or connection resets. Sandbox tokens bypass org-level allowlists in most cases. If you need hosted dev access, open a ticket to have your devbox IP added.
Riley: also try lowering max_tokens and batch_size during dev and add exponential backoff + jitter on 429s. That usually smooths things out.
Priya: rotation question: if I need to rotate a hosted key after a demo, what's the process?
Luis (IT-Sec): request rotation via security-ops@redwood.ai and follow the Console -> API keys -> rotate flow. Hosted keys are treated as high-sensitivity secrets. Rotate immediately if leaked.
Priya: great, thanks all. I'll switch to sandbox locally and open a devex request if demo needs more juice.
